headline: Loss widens on deliberate shift from engineering revenue
summary_short: Sivers Semiconductors' Q2 2026 net sales were SEK 53.8m, down 12% y/y, with EPS of SEK -0.38 (vs -0.19 a year earlier) as adjusted EBITDA widened to SEK -35.5m from SEK -20.9m.
summary_long: Q2 2026 net sales were SEK 53.8m, down 12% y/y (-10% currency-adjusted), as the company deliberately reallocated resources away from NRE (non-recurring engineering) projects toward customer production ramps. Product/hardware revenue rose 18% y/y currency-adjusted, reflecting ramp progress, but wasn't enough to offset the NRE decline. EPS was SEK -0.38 (vs -0.19 y/y); adjusted EBITDA was SEK -35.5m (vs -20.9m y/y). Opportunity pipeline reached USD 1.2B in July, up 268% from year-end 2025. Company expects the transition's financial impact to become visible in Q4 2026 and accelerate through 2027 as multiple programs reach volume production.

The press release's own figure is used as the primary EPS KPI here since it's the company's direct disclosure; the shard discrepancy is flagged rather than silently reconciled. Product/HW revenue growth (+18% y/y) is a rate only — no absolute SEK figure was disclosed, so that row's value is 'n/a'. No sector-specific technology extended metrics (ARR, wafer starts, capex intensity) or universal metrics were disclosed with a clean numeric hit, so extendedMetrics is an empty array; the USD 1.2B opportunity pipeline doesn't map to a defined registry key (distinct from backlog — it's a sales-pipeline figure, not booked orders) and is reported only in the narrative.

drivers.explanation: Company deliberately reallocated resources from NRE projects toward customer production ramps, cutting engineering revenue faster than product/hardware revenue could offset it.
Company says the transition's financial impact should become visible starting Q4 2026 and accelerate through 2027 as multiple programs reach volume production.
